purpose: Pinned VCMI agent client (bridge protocol v2). The MCP/agent layer is expected to adapt to this binary, not the other way around.
frozen_behaviour: state.json: protocol=2, session_id, cmd_seq, ts_wall, in_game, making_turn, date/resources/heroes/towns/objects/query/battle

town/objects JSON: heavy refresh every 2s while allowed; cache miss is read once; load/new-game invalidate caches; the cached town body carries no index - the current town-list index is re-emitted on every tick, so a town-order change can never leak a stale index (non-heavy cache hit included)

results.log: every line produced while a command is executing carries that command's seq=<n> prefix; OK means accepted, not applied. Multi-line replies are normal (e.g. recruit_ui_open then recruit_ui_bought) and asynchronous steps keep the seq of the command that requested them
commands are single-line whitespace-delimited tokens (MCP must never send embedded newlines)

battle: state.json stacks carry shots/counterattacks/defending/waited/double_wide (player-visible combat facts, no hidden HP). battle actions only when it is our stack's turn (else ERR not_my_turn). battle_attack <targetId> [auto|melee|shot] performs a walk-and-attack (engine battleCanAttackUnit + battleCanAttackHex + attack-from hex, so two-hex/long-weapon directions are engine-decided) or a legal shot (battleCanShoot); it never silently becomes a move and refuses with ERR cannot_attack/cannot_melee/cannot_shoot. battle_approach <targetId> is the explicit move-towards action; battle_move validates the destination (ERR illegal_move); battle_actions (read-only) writes battle_actions.json with legal move hexes, per-target can_melee/walk/attack_from/can_shoot and the visible turn order
close_window is safe: refuses to pop when only the root/adventure-map window remains (ERR unsafe_window root)
load_game uses server quickLoadGame; save_game writes Saves/agent/<name>.vsgm1

--agent-start applies <dir>/start_options.txt (H3 advanced options): difficulty, human player color, starting town(FactionID)/hero(HeroTypeID)/bonus, turn/battle/unit timers; logs OK start_option* + OK start_options_effective to results.log

town actions drive the real UI: recruit opens CCastleInterface + CRecruitmentWindow, selects the requested creature card (recruit <town> <level> <amount> [creatureId]; default = the level's base creature), presses BUY 30 frames later and buys exactly the requested amount clamped to available/affordable (the slider is forced with scrollTo because CSlider::setValue ignores its argument in this build); build and garrison transfers open the town screen; it auto-closes ~1.8s after the last town action. Recruit reply lines report creature/amount/requested/dest=hero|town; a BUY that has nothing to buy reports ERR recruit_ui_no_amount (or recruit_ui_no_creature), closes the recruitment window and does not crash the client

probe <heroIdx> x y z [x2 y2 z2 ...] is a read-only path preview: per tile it returns reachable=<0|1> and, when reachable, turns=<n> cost=<movement points> len=<path nodes> teleport=<0|1> embark=<0|1> from the engine path (player-known tiles only; subterranean-gate/teleport and boat transitions are flagged). probe never moves the hero and never flushes a pending UI transaction

read-only diagnostics: ui_tree/probe/ping/battle_actions/town_info/army_info never flush a pending recruit BUY and never close town/puzzle windows; a delayed BUY runs from the frame tick after its 30-frame dwell or when a later mutating command arrives

economy: town_info (read-only, town_info.json) reports every building's engine canBuildStructure state name, cost, affordable/missing_resources, requirement tree (all/any/none of building ids) + missing candidates, mode/upgrade_of/market_building, plus the town market's available modes and RESOURCE_RESOURCE sell->buy give/receive quotes (availability = allowsTrade(RESOURCE_RESOURCE), not the IMarket pointer). army_info (read-only, army_info.json) reports per-slot creature/count and fillUpgradeInfo upgrade options with per-unit costs. split <owner> <idx> <slot> <amount> uses getFreeSlot + splitStack (amount = the new slot's count, must be a strict fraction; the callback return is not an error signal). upgrade <owner> <idx> <slot> <creature> pre-validates legality, target creature and affordability, then reports the actual creature/count/cost. market_trade validates market/mode/resources and reports an estimated receive. build refusals carry the engine state name

client-side info windows are auto-dismissed in agent mode: the obelisk puzzle map (CPuzzleWindow) is shown ~2.5s then closed by the frame tick (results.log: INFO puzzle_map_window), so no manual click is needed

hero observation (T33/P-B, purely additive): state.json heroes also carry mana_max, spellbook (bool), spells[{id,name}], skills[{id,level,name}] (secondary skills, level 1-3), artifacts{worn:[{slot,id,name,locked}],backpack:[{slot,id,name}]}, luck, morale and specialty (name; '' when the hero type has none). Army slots and battle stacks also carry creature_name. Every one of these facts is visible in the normal hero/battle UI; existing keys/order/semantics are unchanged and the protocol stays 2, so an older consumer simply ignores the new fields

battle observation (T33/P-B, additive): state.json battle also carries round (engine round counter), hero_mana / hero_mana_max / hero_spellbook for our fighting hero and cast_spells (how many spells our side has cast in this battle). No hidden enemy data is added
level_up query (T33/P-B, additive): SEC_SKILL options carry the secondary-skill name in `name` next to the numeric `sub` id; the answer index semantics are unchanged

adventure-map magic (T35): heroJson spells[] entries also carry cost (hero->getSpellCost), adventure (bool) and can_cast (mana >= cost). cast_spell <heroIdx> <spellId> [x y z] is the adventure spellbook request: the bridge requires an adventure spell known in the spellbook, checks the engine's adventure canBeCast/canBeCastAt problems and mana, passes int3(-1,-1,-1) for no-target spells and the given tile for ranged spells, then calls CCallback::castSpell. Refusals are explicit ERR not_adventure_spell / spell_not_known / not_enough_mana / adventure_cast_blocked / target_required / bad_target

battle magic (T35): battle_actions.json also carries hero{mana,mana_max,spellbook,can_cast,reason,casts_used} and spells[{id,name,cost,can_cast,reason,target_kind}] where target_kind is none|unit|hex|unsupported and every fact comes from the engine (battleCanCastSpell / battleGetSpellCost / getCasterAction). battle_cast_spell <spellId> [unit <stackId>|hex <x> <y>] builds the same BattleAction the battle spellbook sends (EActionType::HERO_SPELL, stackNumber=-1, side=battleGetMySide(), aimToHex) and sends it with CBattleCallback::battleMakeSpellAction; it refuses ERR no_battle/no_hero/bad_spell/not_combat_spell/spell_not_known/no_active_stack/not_my_turn/cast_blocked/spell_cannot_be_cast/not_enough_mana/target_required/no_target_stack/bad_hex/spell_target_unsupported. Two-stage spells (Teleport/Sacrifice) are rejected deterministically BEFORE any legality/target resolution: spellById recognises the spell (SpellID 63/40, plus the stable config identifiers teleport/sacrifice for mod variants) and the bridge answers ERR spell_target_unsupported <spellname> two_stage without building or submitting a BattleAction and without spending mana (never OK). battle_actions spells[] marks them can_cast=false / reason=two_stage_unsupported / two_stage=true (additive; other rows unchanged). The two-target sequence itself is not implemented

debug cheat channel (T35, test-only, env-gated): when the launcher exports AUTO_HEROS3_CHEAT_FILE, the server polls that file every 200ms and applies lines <resource> <amount>, allspells <heroIdx|all>, learnspell <heroIdx|all> <spellId>, mana <heroIdx|all> <amount>. Inert without the env variable (normal runs unaffected). The MCP exposes no spell/mana cheat tool; this channel is for isolated live tests only

coordinates (T40/C11, purely additive): hero/object/town JSON carry `anchor` (= pos, the sprite anchor) and `tile` (= visitable, the interaction/visit tile that pathfinding and object visits use) next to the unchanged `pos`/`visitable`; the two differ by the map object's visitable offset (e.g. hero anchor (34,33) vs interaction tile (32,33)) - that is engine semantics, not an off-by-one. Moves/visits/paths compare `tile`; the MCP digest and game_brief pass the compact `tile` through. Legacy consumers that only read pos/visitable are unaffected

recruit_hero (T40/C11): the bridge pre-checks the server's HeroPoolProcessor::hireHero conditions and answers ERR recruit_hero_refused <reason> (visiting_hero | no_tavern | enemy_town | not_enough_gold | hero_cap_on_map | hero_cap_total) instead of the old misleading OK (the server refuses those cases through CGameHandler::complain - an INFO text, no reply packet). bad_town_index / no_such_available_hero are unchanged. A successful command still only submits the asynchronous hire: OK recruit_hero town=<i> index=<j> name=<hero> cost=2500 gold_before=<n>; the MCP verifies the outcome as a state diff (new hero and/or gold spent) and never retries a possibly-paid hire

open_hero <heroIdx> (T40/C11): opens the real hero screen through CPlayerInterface::openHeroWindow (a CHeroWindow - its class name appears in the ui_tree dump). The window is deliberately left open so it can be screenshotted/recorded; close_window_safe accepts CHeroWindow and pops it exactly like the window's own close button. ERR bad_hero_index when the index is not in getHeroesInfo()

ui_tree freshness (T42/F1, MCP-side rule; audit 2026-10-27): ui_tree dumps are bound to the command that requests them. The MCP verifier for open_hero only reports completed when the bridge ui_tree query itself succeeded (OK) AND <state-dir>/ui_tree.json was refreshed by that query (file signature mtime_ns/size/sha256 must change after the request). An UNKNOWN/REJECTED query, a query that leaves the file unchanged, or a missing file is reported as unknown and creates an unresolved gate - a CHeroWindow left in an older dump is NEVER accepted as a fresh observation. The window itself is still left open on any verdict
check_policy: agent start() hashes the exe and warns (does not refuse) when it differs from this file; it also warns when the client source files differ between built_from_commit and HEAD. A protocol mismatch is a hard error. Update this file deliberately when the client is rebuilt.
